pillar_reactions.evidence: Delivered in full from 00:33:00 — onboarding call, custom programme, film-and-correct video loop on every new movement, weekly check-in form, app logging, weekly programme updates with the reasoning explained, plus five to ten minutes of prescribed morning mobility. Asked for questions he said 'No I love it', and when asked what he liked he volunteered his own corroborating experience rather than just agreeing: 'the guys that I trained with in Byron Bay would do 20 minutes mobility, 90 90s, a lot of hip opening stuff... when I was doing that regularly I was feeling so good. It just made such a difference to my training. Not even my training, but just day-to-day.' The video correction loop in particular answered a need he had already named — wanting feedback so he is 'not kooking it and doing myself damage'.

Delivered from 00:37:24 — no calorie tracking, three to five governing principles, intermittent fasting, a protein floor of roughly a pound of meat and six eggs, whole foods in the eating window. The rep pre-framed it as the low-priority pillar for this prospect and it landed that way: 'No, I've used intermittent fasting a fair bit and it's definitely achieved results.' Understood and agreed with no questions and no objection. Notable that the rep still used nutrition to open a gap — 'you're eating super healthy, but we're also not at a place where we're super happy with our physique' — and the prospect did not contest it.

Delivered from 00:39:36 — structure removing decision load, Trevor's phone number both ways, a text if a workout is missed, weekly check-ins, a community of executives and consultants, regular group coaching calls and weekly live Zoom workout classes. Reaction was the warmest of the three: 'No, no, I think it's really important. I think that's the thing where it falls away, right? I do enjoy training with other people... it's no questions. It's just, I think it's a positive.' And when asked what stood out most across the entire presentation he named this pillar unprompted: 'I think the important parts, the community accountability is a big factor.' He also flagged the flexibility of async plus optional live as a specific plus.

anchors.raw: a week to week thing was is somewhere i've always sat beforehand... you commit to a three-month project and it's like here's your weekly costs while we do that
anchors.note: The dominant anchor. He arrived expecting a month-to-month or week-to-week engagement and said so repeatedly, including 'initially, I was thinking it could be a month-to-month' and 'it doesn't need a completely personalized program initially.' A single upfront six-month figure was not a bigger number than he could pay, it was a different commercial shape than he had modelled. This is what the call actually died on, and the payment plan the playbook provides was never offered against it.

anchors.raw: off the U.S. dollars alone, it's okay, but then by the time you translate it into Australian dollars, it's like, oh, that's probably a bit more than what I was thinking
anchors.note: The rep converted live to roughly AUD 8,600. The USD figure was acceptable to him and the AUD figure was not, which is a soft anchor worth tracking across the corpus for non-US prospects — the same offer clears one bar and fails another purely on presentation currency.

anchors.raw: I don't want to go along and find elements of things that I like for myself and piece it together... I believe in expertise. That's my, my job is, I've had, you know, top 10 restaurants in the country
anchors.note: A strong supporting anchor that was never leveraged. He is himself an expert who charges for 6-12 month full-time consulting engagements, he distanced himself explicitly from people trying to glean knowledge cheaply, and his partner runs an instructor-training business. He also pre-emptively rejected the discount frame — 'this isn't me trying to get... a taste of this'. The rep had a prospect who buys expertise for a living and answered him with a discount.

anchors.raw: If it's projected and it's like, okay... A class in level one kettlebells, or level two kettlebells, or level four kettlebells, and you have one-on-one coaching, here's your program, you are part of that process, and here's an upfront cost, then I'd walk in and be like, okay, cool, this is the expectation of what is required to take part in this program.
anchors.note: He named the frame under which he would accept the same upfront cost without resistance. He is mid-way through a freediving instructor qualification and reasons about paid learning in those terms. The offer was described to him as 'you're going to university for kettlebells' but sold as a transformation package, and the gap between those two framings is precisely where he stalled.

unmet_demand.want: A staged product — three programme blocks across six months with the education and mastery layer on the back end, entered incrementally rather than committed to in full up front
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The only SKU is a single six-month one-to-one bundle with the mastery framing front-loaded. He described the alternative in unusual detail when asked what a ten out of ten looked like: 'it would probably just be a program that's written, like, in three stages over six months. And then I would love an educational side on the tail end of it. I think front-loading education is a bit tricky.' There is no such offer to sell him.

unmet_demand.want: To spread the outlay rather than pay a single upfront sum, having twice named month-to-month or week-to-week as his expectation
unmet_demand.why_unmet: Nothing about the programme prevents this — the playbook's money play explicitly contains 'Most clients pay upfront, but for some we break it up. Want to explore making it work?' and other calls in the corpus have closed on instalments. It was simply never offered. The prospect was left believing a lump sum was the only way in.

unmet_demand.want: Written options with prices he can assess in his own time before committing
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The process withholds price until the call and presents one figure verbally. He named the mismatch directly: 'it's like walking into a restaurant without a menu and a price list, you know? So it's like I want to be able to figure out where I fit within that.' The rep agreed to email options afterwards, which concedes the point but only after the close had already failed.

unmet_demand.want: A formalised, credentialled progression — named levels he could work through and point to, comparable to the freediving instructor qualification he is currently completing
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The programme is coaching with a mastery narrative attached, not a certification, and the rep confirmed as much implicitly by never offering one when the prospect raised it three separate times. He was explicit that he was not demanding accreditation — 'I'm not saying it's like a formal educational thing' — but the levelled structure is what would have made the price legible to him.
